edges.rationale: The required deterministic properties disproved retrieval as the canonical representation.
A separate source tree preserved the representation boundary.
A staged compiler required a source-structure representation before semantics.
Coordinate-aware reconstruction replaced raw text order.
Multiple evidence classes replaced style-only inference.
The tree contract requires exact source spans and locations.
Coordinate-aware blocks made source-bound ArticleSeeds possible.
Contextual NEC grammar replaced universal marker promotion.
Ownership and scope required explicit representation.
Flat selected fragments exposed the need for printed hierarchy.
Stable clause ownership enabled semantic review.
Development records were retained as evidence, not promoted to issued text.
Parser errors can only be separated from source changes using independent edition evidence.
Repository-owned adaptation preserved reproducibility and source boundaries.
Reference material may inform design without becoming runtime coupling.
Neutral primitives replaced universal grammar as the reuse boundary.
Style profiles demonstrated legitimate edition-specific parsing.
IBC tested which concepts were shared and which were NEC-specific.
IBC layout and hierarchy behavior justified separate family grammars.
NFPA 13 added annex and external-reference evidence against universal grammar.
A linked-corpus boundary preserves distinct source semantics.
Target domains permit code references to external technical corpora.
Support claims must follow reproducible tests and current tree state.
Using the upstream workflow replaced the local facsimile.
LORE maintains accepted current knowledge while Deciduous records causal evolution.
Shared contracts and family grammars define the current durable model.
Durable downstream references exposed the mismatch between code identity and artifact pagination.
Separating publication structure from semantic interpretation made the code's own hierarchy available as the stable coordinate layer.
The user-facing and cross-edition coordinate should match how the code is actually cited.
Independent issued editions must be compared by structural address and explicit renumbering relationships rather than page movement.
Once structural addresses are primary, page coordinates remain useful only as source-artifact provenance.

nodes.description: Downstream systems needed stable code structure that could be compared, referenced, validated, and traced back to a specific publication, rather than a search result or prose summary.
nodes.title: Create a deterministic machine-legible building-code representation

nodes.description: A retrieval or summary layer could answer questions quickly, but it could not provide deterministic hierarchy, stable identities, exact source spans, or reproducible structural comparisons.
nodes.title: Treat search, RAG, or summarization as the code representation

nodes.description: Building Code Map, edition comparison, amendment overlays, and future reasoning require provisions with durable location and provenance so retrieval does not become authority.
nodes.title: Downstream code analysis needs addressable provisions, not merely relevant passages

nodes.description: The repository would transform source artifacts into publication structure and then selected semantic representations, while preserving unsupported or ambiguous language instead of inventing meaning.
nodes.title: Build a staged compiler rather than a search index

nodes.description: The project owns deterministic source structure and parser evidence. Retrieval, jurisdiction selection, and compliance conclusions remain downstream concerns.
nodes.title: Building Code AST became a source-structure and evidence layer

nodes.description: An AST can identify and transform an edition, but it does not make the derived structure authoritative, establish adoption, or replace official text and AHJ judgment.
nodes.title: Separate technical representation from legal authority

nodes.description: The initial provision parser proved exact semantic spans were possible, but it could not express chapters, nested lists, definitions, tables, or document-level hierarchy.
nodes.title: Represent publication structure before interpreting rule meaning

nodes.description: Modality, threshold, action, and exception fields were useful for a bounded sentence, yet document ingestion required a separate tree that did not prematurely assign semantics.
nodes.title: A provision-first AST could not carry full document organization

nodes.description: This would make every structural parser imply semantic correctness and force code-family layout facts into a meaning-oriented schema.
nodes.title: Put publication hierarchy and interpreted rule meaning in one universal tree

nodes.description: The Document AST records source artifact, edition, recursive structural nodes, stable identities, exact spans, and diagnostics while excluding modality, conditions, actions, and compliance fields.
nodes.title: Create an independently versioned Document AST

nodes.description: Stable identifiers survive reparsing of the same edition while changing when the publication identity changes; source text and offsets remain evidence rather than identity inputs.
nodes.title: Derive node identity from artifact, edition, node type, and structural locator

nodes.description: Document, chapter, section, subsection, paragraph, list item, definition entry, table parts, headings, notes, footnotes, and unsupported structures form the common vocabulary without claiming a common grammar.
nodes.title: Shared document primitives became the neutral contract

nodes.description: Source PDFs expose text, coordinates, outlines, and visual layout unevenly. The parser needed to retain enough evidence to reconstruct reading order without confusing extraction order with code hierarchy.
nodes.title: Recover printed structure from imperfect PDF evidence

nodes.description: Headers, footers, columns, continuation pages, glyph runs, and table fragments made text order an unreliable proxy for printed or logical hierarchy.
nodes.title: Treat the PDF text stream as document hierarchy

nodes.description: NEC required two-column block ordering and article boundaries; IBC exposed glyph-level spacing, superscripts, mixed table-and-column bands, and recurring page furniture.
nodes.title: Coordinates and reading order are evidence, not the final tree

nodes.description: Visual style helps identify candidates but cannot safely distinguish continuations, wrapped titles, list levels, columns, or publisher furniture across editions.
nodes.title: Infer hierarchy from font size or indentation alone

nodes.description: Layout adapters retain source coordinates and normalized character spans so every structural claim can be audited against the source region that produced it.
nodes.title: Preserve page, geometry, extraction span, and exclusion evidence

nodes.description: Unknown table boundaries, malformed markers, and unresolved reading order remain visible evidence. Successful extraction is never inferred from silent omission.
nodes.title: Keep ambiguous or unsupported layout as diagnostics instead of discarding it

nodes.description: The first real source slice had to prove local, source-safe ingestion, exact article boundaries, provenance, and deterministic private outputs without publishing licensed text.
nodes.title: Use the supplied 2017 NEC PDF to exercise real code ingestion

nodes.description: The public repository contains parser code, schemas, tests, and documentation; PDFs, extracted prose, page images, source hashes, and generated ArticleSeeds remain private.
nodes.title: Keep NEC source artifacts and text-bearing outputs local

nodes.description: The initial production slice exercised scope and language policy, definitions, general requirements, exceptions, notes, and one table-like region while keeping whole-edition support out of scope.
nodes.title: Validate Articles 90, 100, and 110 before claiming broader coverage

nodes.description: The optional PyMuPDF adapter discovers article bookmarks, trims same-page transitions, orders blocks, emits source maps, and validates Document AST spans.
nodes.title: Build source-bound private NEC ArticleSeeds

nodes.description: Production smoke tests and later selected-fragment review corrected boundaries and classifications that synthetic fixtures alone could not reveal.
nodes.title: Fragment review exposed article transitions, definition candidates, and table-like blocks

nodes.description: Main supports local ingestion and hierarchy/semantic processing for the exercised selected articles. It does not claim every article, table, figure, annex, or edition.
nodes.title: NEC 2017 support is real but intentionally bounded

nodes.description: Flat ArticleSeed blocks were not enough for stable locators, parent-child validation, selected semantic review, or clause comparison.
nodes.title: Reconstruct NEC articles, parts, sections, subdivisions, lists, notes, and exceptions

nodes.description: Titled subdivisions may share blocks; repeated marker classes can recur at different depths; Article 100 parentheticals can resemble list markers.
nodes.title: PDF blocks merge and split NEC clauses differently from printed hierarchy

nodes.description: The same syntax can represent structural subdivisions, ordinary lists, units, or definition text, and marker meaning changes with context and edition.
nodes.title: Treat every parenthetical marker as a universal hierarchy token

nodes.description: The hierarchy builder uses Part and Section identities, title evidence, list introductions, marker ancestry, source order, and ambiguity diagnostics rather than syntax alone.
nodes.title: Use NEC-specific hierarchy rules with contextual evidence

nodes.description: The private reference validates parser output and reveals mismatches but does not repair output, enter generated artifacts, or become required at runtime.
nodes.title: Use the prior junk-drawer NEC hierarchy as a conformance oracle, not a dependency

nodes.description: Style guidance helps interpret definition placement, parallel numbering, titles, and note identity, but the published edition remains source evidence and ambiguous markers remain unresolved.
nodes.title: Use edition-aware NEC Style Manual profiles as parser priors and validation context

nodes.description: The reviewed Article 90 and 110 structural records matched the local oracle; Article 100 produced no false numbered-clause records in that comparison.
nodes.title: Selected NEC hierarchy matched the independent oracle without runtime coupling

nodes.description: Meaning depends on ownership, order, exceptions, conditions, definitions, references, and surrounding source, not just the sentence containing a modal verb.
nodes.title: Preserve clause context before deriving normative meaning

nodes.description: A continuation paragraph may belong to a printed clause; an exception can modify an ancestor; a definition or table can govern distant provisions through references.
nodes.title: Printed hierarchy, logical hierarchy, and normative dependency are not identical

nodes.description: Flattening preserves words but destroys ownership, ordering, scope, and the distinction between normative and explanatory material.
nodes.title: Flatten exceptions, notes, subordinate lists, and definitions into paragraphs

nodes.description: Shared structural node types and code-family metadata preserve source organization while exceptions and semantic clause roles remain in later family-specific stages where evidence supports them.
nodes.title: Represent definitions, lists, notes, tables, footnotes, and unsupported regions explicitly

nodes.description: References retain source spans and target locators or target domains; unresolved references remain unresolved rather than being forced into the current document.
nodes.title: Preserve references as evidence-backed relationships rather than copied text

nodes.description: Article 100 definitions and Sections 90.5, 110.2, 110.3, 110.14, 110.16, and 110.26 preserve clauses, exceptions, notes, references, tags, and exact spans without claiming compliance interpretation.
nodes.title: Selected NEC clauses gained reviewable semantic projections

nodes.description: A parser difference between 2017 and 2020 could reflect amended text, layout drift, missing content, or a parser defect; the evidence streams must remain independent.
nodes.title: Distinguish actual NEC edition changes from extraction errors

nodes.description: Summaries can identify candidates but omit rejected proposals, procedural reversals, errata, and exact issued text.
nodes.title: Treat secondary change summaries as authoritative edition deltas

nodes.description: Public inputs, comments, actions, TIAs, errata, and Council outcomes can predict where change should appear, but only as process evidence.
nodes.title: Use NFPA development records to build an expected-change oracle

nodes.description: Expected changes cannot fabricate observed 2020 text. The 2017 and 2020 parsers must run independently before reconciliation.
nodes.title: Treat independently observed issued editions as controlling text evidence

nodes.description: The expected-change machinery could be exercised, but observed-change reconciliation remained blocked without a lawful source artifact.
nodes.title: Authorized 2020 NEC source was not available for reconciliation

nodes.description: The branch models process evidence and diagnostics, but main does not claim a 2020 parser, a complete changelog, or observed edition reconciliation.
nodes.title: NEC 2020 expected changelog remains branch-bound and non-authoritative

nodes.description: IBC provided a second major code family to test whether the NEC machinery reflected shared document concepts or NEC-specific accidents.
nodes.title: Adapt the compiler to the supplied 2018 IBC PDF

nodes.description: That would couple public operation to private code, obscure provenance, and make the repository unreproducible for other users.
nodes.title: Import the prior private PDF parser as a runtime dependency

nodes.description: Geometry, reading-order, source-map, and validation ideas were reimplemented in repository-owned code with synthetic public tests and private source execution.
nodes.title: Adapt useful parser architecture without taking a private dependency

nodes.description: The source required visual-baseline grouping, word-boundary repair, hyphenation evidence, page-local reading modes, and table exclusion before structural parsing.
nodes.title: IBC exposed glyph-oriented text, spacing defects, mixed columns, tables, scripts, and publisher furniture

nodes.description: The branch exercised opening matter, administrative provisions, hundreds of definitions, and ruled tables while failing closed for unsupported chapters.
nodes.title: Limit the initial IBC production slice to Chapters 1 through 3

nodes.description: Decimal section parents, Parts, enumerations, exceptions, definitions, tables, figures, notes, and appendix-prefixed locators require ICC conventions rather than NEC marker rules.
nodes.title: Design an IBC-specific hierarchy builder over neutral primitives

nodes.description: The layout branch has substantial private-source validation, but the ingestion and hierarchy stack remains unmerged; complete-edition and appendix support are not claimed.
nodes.title: IBC findings changed the architecture without becoming current main support

nodes.description: NEC, ICC, and NFPA publications share provenance and tree concepts but differ materially in numbering, editorial conventions, annexes, tables, and layout.
nodes.title: Share parser machinery without pretending all code families use one grammar

nodes.description: Universal marker and numbering assumptions would misclassify lists, parts, decimal sections, annex correspondences, and edition-specific layout.
nodes.title: Use one grammar for NEC, IBC, and NFPA documents

nodes.description: Publication-neutral primitives provide interoperability and validation without deciding how a source family recognizes those structures.
nodes.title: Share source identity, spans, diagnostics, tables, and generic node contracts

nodes.description: Each family can evolve its parser and evidence rules without destabilizing the neutral AST or claiming support for unrelated editions.
nodes.title: Keep NEC, IBC, ICC evidence, and NFPA grammars separately versioned

nodes.description: A source-family parser may select an edition profile or fail closed; premature normalization is less trustworthy than explicit compatibility limits.
nodes.title: Permit edition-specific profiles when evidence shows layout or editorial change

nodes.description: Shared layout/evidence utilities feed source-family adapters and hierarchy builders; current support claims are expressed per source family, edition, and validated region.
nodes.title: The architecture became neutral at contracts and specific at grammars

nodes.description: NFPA 13 tested chapters, nested numbered clauses, annex explanations, external-standard references, revision markers, and table geometry beyond the NEC slice.
nodes.title: Investigate and parse the 2019 NFPA 13 clause hierarchy

nodes.description: The branch could publish source-safe code, schemas, reviewed non-reconstructive cases, and aggregate receipts but not the PDF or full text-bearing bundle.
nodes.title: NFPA 13 source access and generated text had to remain local

nodes.description: The branch records producer commit, engine and wrapper identity, environment, source ownership, spans, relationships, diagnostics, and deterministic output.
nodes.title: Use a provenance-pinned local extractor and strict bundle contract

nodes.description: Only explicit Annex A correspondence nodes can emit an explains relationship; parent containers must not manufacture semantic links.
nodes.title: Synthesized Annex A ancestry containers are structural, not explanatory relationships

nodes.description: NFPA, ASTM, ASME, AWWA, ANSI, UL, IEEE, and ISO citations cannot all be treated as locators in NFPA 13; unresolved ownership remains explicit.
nodes.title: Distinguish internal, external-standard, and unspecified-document targets

nodes.description: The branch preserves table subtrees and diagnostics but does not infer semantic spans, units, figure meaning, or engineering interpretation from layout alone.
nodes.title: Table geometry can be conservative while figure and diagram semantics remain unsupported

nodes.description: Complete-source deterministic validation on the draft is strong evidence for the branch, not evidence that main currently supports NFPA 13 or every construct.
nodes.title: NFPA 13 demonstrated broader scalability but remains unmerged

nodes.description: Listings, categories, certification files, marking guidance, and product observations are not prescriptive model-code clauses even when code provisions reference them.
nodes.title: Determine how UL White Book and related technical sources should connect to code structure

nodes.description: These entities need temporal and evidentiary relationships that do not fit a chapter-section-clause tree.
nodes.title: UL source records model categories, certifications, products, holders, and dated observations

nodes.description: This would collapse prescriptive code structure, reference material, certification state, and equipment lineage into one misleading tree.
nodes.title: Put UL categories and certifications directly into the building-code document AST

nodes.description: That repository owns the source-specific compiler, CCN index, Product iQ snapshots, equipment relationships, and publication boundary.
nodes.title: Keep UL White Book compilation and certification lineage in Electrical Equipment Lineage

nodes.description: Building Code AST can preserve a citation and target domain; a related ontology or graph can resolve that target to listing, product, or certification evidence.
nodes.title: Let code AST nodes link to external technical corpora without absorbing their models

nodes.description: The code tree stays focused on source structure. Exact interchange identities and ontology semantics remain future evidence-backed design work.
nodes.title: The ownership boundary is active while the cross-corpus link model remains open

nodes.description: Parser output must identify what source, edition, region, parser, and transformation produced it and what remains uncertain or unreviewed.
nodes.title: Make every derived structure auditable without confusing it with authoritative source text

nodes.description: Structural claims remain traceable to the evidence from which they were derived, including source coordinates when the adapter can supply them.
nodes.title: Record source artifact, edition, page or region, printed locator, and exact extraction span

nodes.description: Confidence is a review aid, not a legal probability; deterministic lexical methods and explicit review status are preferable to unlabeled inference.
nodes.title: Record parser version, transformation history, diagnostics, and review state where contracts support them

nodes.description: A source may be available to the owner without permission to redistribute it. Registration guards exact bytes and records restricted or uncertain publication boundaries.
nodes.title: Separate evidence role, access scope, and rights status

nodes.description: Generated structure can be deterministic and reviewed while the issued publication remains controlling. Development history, errata, and amendments retain their own evidence roles.
nodes.title: Label ASTs, expected changelogs, and projections as derived evidence

nodes.description: Public Git contains project-authored software, schemas, documentation, diagnostics, aggregate receipts, and synthetic fixtures rather than copyrighted source corpora.
nodes.title: The repository publishes contracts and synthetic evidence while text-bearing outputs stay private

nodes.description: Unsupported regions, unresolved references, blocked action chains, and diagnostics keep absence from masquerading as successful parsing.
nodes.title: Preserve malformed, ambiguous, or unsupported content instead of dropping it

nodes.description: A parser is trustworthy only when its output is deterministic, source-located, structurally legal, and bounded to the regions actually reviewed.
nodes.title: Validate parser claims against source evidence and invariants

nodes.description: Production audits check retained and excluded fragments, source spans, reading order, hierarchy records, and representative golden cases without publishing source prose.
nodes.title: Compare extracted fragments against source locations and known-good references

nodes.description: Document and family-specific validators reject duplicate locators, out-of-parent spans, malformed ancestry, unresolved required parents, and nondeterministic identities.
nodes.title: Enforce identity, span, containment, uniqueness, ordering, and parent-child invariants

nodes.description: A table boundary, a semantic table interpretation, a figure reference, and a resolved target are different claims and receive different checks or diagnostics.
nodes.title: Validate table partitions, figure support claims, and cross-reference resolution separately

nodes.description: Synthetic fixtures make contracts reproducible; private exact-source runs expose real layout defects; neither alone proves complete-edition support.
nodes.title: Use public synthetic fixtures and private source replay together

nodes.description: ICC proposal/action separation, Washington leaf-span layout, sequence preservation, and unsupported-action boundaries required multiple post-merge corrections.
nodes.title: Official corpus replay exposed adapter defects after initial implementation

nodes.description: Open or superseded branch results are recorded as branch evidence; current support is never inferred from a PR description alone.
nodes.title: Reconcile PR claims against merge state, current tree, tests, and generated outputs

nodes.description: The AST should expose stable evidence-bearing structures that downstream systems can combine with their own authority and domain models.
nodes.title: Keep source structure reusable without absorbing jurisdiction, product lineage, or compliance logic

nodes.description: A code clause cannot determine which jurisdiction or edition applies to an address; that requires geocoding, boundary resolution, policy evidence, and time-aware adoption data.
nodes.title: Building Code Map owns location, authority, adoption, amendment applicability, and permit-context resolution

nodes.description: Code references can connect to that corpus, but certification history and equipment compatibility remain separate evidence domains.
nodes.title: Electrical Equipment Lineage owns manufacturer, product, UL, and replacement evidence

nodes.description: The repository can represent add, replace, delete, reserve, and scope evidence without deciding the governing jurisdiction or rendering a legally controlling consolidated code.
nodes.title: Model jurisdictional amendments as source-backed patches against an identified base publication state

nodes.description: Future tools may resolve definitions, conditions, exceptions, amendments, products, and project facts, but they must consume provenance rather than mutate the canonical source tree.
nodes.title: Keep compliance and engineering reasoning out of the source-structure repository

nodes.description: Downstream products can compare clauses, reconcile expected changes, resolve amendments, and link technical corpora while this repository preserves source structure and parser truthfulness.
nodes.title: Building Code AST remains a bounded compiler and evidence substrate

nodes.description: As the repository accumulated source families and branch experiments, its documentation needed accepted history, generated views, and exact-head verification without duplicating another knowledge system.
nodes.title: Make architecture decisions, parser limits, and verification evidence maintainable

nodes.description: The first interpretation duplicated LORE rather than using its shipped skill and transaction model, creating a parallel maintenance mechanism.
nodes.title: Recreate LORE-style records and renderers inside the repository

nodes.description: The repository pins the trust root, records accepted semantic history and a transaction receipt, and generates non-authoritative projections through LORE.
nodes.title: Adopt LORE itself and its shipped maintenance skill

nodes.description: The graph explains why models and parser boundaries changed. Repository code, schemas, tests, accepted LORE records, and source publications remain authoritative for current behavior.
nodes.title: Add Deciduous as a non-authoritative causal archaeology layer

nodes.description: Main contains Document AST, Provision AST 0.2.0, NEC Articles 90/100/110 ingestion and hierarchy/semantics, source register, ICC errata/development adapters, and Washington amendment adapters.
nodes.title: Current main supports shared AST contracts, selected NEC 2017 workflows, and publication evidence adapters

nodes.description: These branches contain substantial work or design evidence, but none may be labeled current main support or complete-edition coverage.
nodes.title: IBC 2018, NFPA 13 2019, NEC 2020 expected changes, and Provision AST 0.3 remain branch-bound

nodes.description: New datasets expand evidence only after source-safe ingestion, family grammar, deterministic projections, source review, and support-claim qualification. Open research remains marked unresolved.
nodes.title: The durable contract is provenance-first, family-specific, fail-closed, and explicitly bounded

nodes.description: PDF pagination varies across editions, printings, and source files, while the publication's own section hierarchy is the durable coordinate engineers use.
nodes.title: Engineers navigate and cite code by sections and subsections, not PDF pages

nodes.description: Sections, subsections, tables, figures, exceptions, definitions, and equations become canonical navigation coordinates. Page numbers cannot supply fallback structural identities.
nodes.title: Make published code addresses the primary identity and navigation surface

nodes.description: PDF pages, printed-page labels, offsets, bounding boxes, and raw block locators remain available for source reproduction and parser debugging, while navigation, relationships, ordering, and edition comparison use structural code addresses.
nodes.title: Retain PDF coordinates only as secondary provenance

nodes.description: PRs #15, #17, and #18 were provisional development stages. They established extraction and review evidence but were superseded rather than merged after the consolidated corpus closeout.
nodes.title: IBC 2018 evolved through stacked structural, inventory, and closeout branches

nodes.description: PR #33 merged the source-safe IBC 2018 corpus, actual-record-shape section indexing, deterministic validation, and the decision that code addresses are primary while pages remain provenance.
nodes.title: Merge the source-backed IBC 2018 corpus with section-first navigation

nodes.description: PR #20 supplied the reviewed extraction design, source boundary, complete-source receipts, and provenance defect discovery. Its stacked branch was closed after a clean transplant.
nodes.title: Retain NFPA 13 PR #20 as the detailed review record

nodes.description: PR #34 preserved the reviewed NFPA 13 hierarchy, strict bundle, schemas, cases, and tools while enforcing checkout and producer-file provenance.
nodes.title: Merge verified NFPA 13 support on a clean current-main branch

nodes.description: PR #19 established the source-safe expected-change and reconciliation contracts. Its old branch was superseded after a conflict-free transplant.
nodes.title: Retain NEC 2020 PR #19 as the expected-change review record

nodes.description: PR #35 merged deterministic development-record expectations and reconciliation machinery. Actual observed-edition reconciliation remains gated on an authorized 2020 NEC source artifact.
nodes.title: Merge the NEC 2020 expected-change framework without inventing observed text

nodes.description: PR #12 contains the original reviewed design and PR #36 the first clean transplant. Both were superseded when main advanced during verification.
nodes.title: Preserve the reviewed composable-condition branches as historical evidence

nodes.description: PR #37 merged recursive nullable condition expressions, homogeneous all_of and any_of parsing, strict rejection boundaries, schema updates, fixtures, and tests.
nodes.title: Merge Provision AST 0.3 composable condition expressions
